summary: A woman named Trish meets Damian, a former partner who is now her colleague in a professional role, at his office after a meeting about a discussion draft of a bill. She declines to send him a copy, suggests he get one from the Navy man present, and leaves. Outside, Damian expresses regret over their past relationship, and Trish firmly steers the exchange back to professionalism, finally giving him a comforting hug before sending him back inside. The excerpt ends with her returning home, pouring a small glass of rare Irish whisky, and receiving a phone call.
one_line: Trish firmly sets professional boundaries with her former partner Damian after a meeting about a bill, then returns home to a phone call.
key_facts: Damian admits he did not know the discussion draft of the bill existed until the meeting.
Trish says she would offer to send Damian a copy of the discussion draft but expects it would take a week to arrive, if it ever did.
Trish suggests Damian ask the Navy man for a copy of the discussion draft, saying the man looks like he knows his way around.
Trish tells Damian to drop by her office if he wants to chat about the bill.
Trish says "Good luck settling in" as she leaves.
Damian hugs Trish, which she finds weird because hugging is strictly west-of-the-Mississippi, and she breaks it off firmly.
The first snows are coming in and the steps are slightly icy when Trish leaves.
Damian says "I've never been happy the way I was with you" and "I haven't been that happy since."
Trish left Damian to come east and do something he thought of as wrong-headed, backwards and superstitious.
Trish tells Damian: "You're here to do a job, and your job requires that you and I keep it on a professional level."
Trish gives Damian a long, soulful hug on the street, then sends him back toward his office.
That afternoon Trish's phone starts ringing normally, her outbound calls connect, her email is delivered, and her car gets her home in record time.
Trish pours herself a very small glass of Irish whisky so rare that it had been known to make grown men weep.
Trish normally saves the whisky for celebrations, but says she is damned if she knows what she is celebrating.
